newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rate cuts drove down Australian CPI -Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rate cuts drove down Australian CPI -Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Wednesday said the fall in the inflation rate in the December quarter was mostly due to last year's monetary policy easings.
"The reason why it's falling -- the headline rate -- is that we have had the interest rate reductions," he said on Perth radio 6PR.
"The major reason why they're falling is mortgage interest rates -- charges -- have fallen, negative 7.6 percent."
Earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said its consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the December quarter to stand 1.5 percent above its level of a year before.
Excluding such large irregulars as mortgage interest charges to produce an estimate of underlying inflation, prices rose 0.4 percent in the quarter and 2.1 percent over the year.
The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy three times between July and December, each time dropping its target for overnight cash rates by 0.5 percentage point.
Overnight cash is now around 6.0 percent.
